preamble: Loss of the alveolar implosive: [ɗ] disappears. Gravina (2014) describes Proto-Central Chadic *ɗ as "frequently reduced to /ʔ/ or lost altogether". In Proto-Tera *ɗ was deleted word-finally. Word-initial *ɗ was lost in a single word, *ɗɨɬɨj 'egg', in several languages: Mbuko ɬaj and Mandara ɬaja show no trace of it, while Mafa ɬaɬaj reduplicates the next consonant.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Central Chadic to Mbuko and Mandara

examples.note: Gravina (2014: 64), example (65). Merey and Gemzek ɗəɬaʸ keep ɗ, and Mafa ɬaɬaj compensates by reduplication. The sources consulted give only this one example.
